Description: Lets an authenticated student see live instrument availability and hold a slot of at most 2 hours, up to 7 days ahead, on an instrument whose calibration is valid. Traces to FR-001.
Makes calibration state gate bookability rather than merely be displayed, so no reading is ever taken on an out-of-calibration instrument. Traces to FR-002.
Ties physical custody of an instrument to the booking record through token validation and server-side check-out and check-in timestamps. Traces to FR-003.
Implements the disciplinary rule: overdue computation, a 30-minute grace window, strikes, and suspension on the third strike inside a rolling 30 days. Traces to FR-004.
Recovers scarce lab capacity from abandoned bookings instead of leaving instruments idle. Traces to FR-005.
Platform integrity: role-based access, an append-only evidence trail, and correct isolation on the contended reservation write. Traces to NFR-001 and NFR-002.
Gives the Faculty Supervisor visibility of how lab capacity is actually used. Traces to UC-13.
As a student, I want to see live availability for every instrument across the next 7 days, so that I can pick a free slot without walking to the lab.
As a student, I want to reserve a slot of up to 2 hours on a calibrated instrument, so that the instrument is guaranteed free when I arrive.
As a lab administrator, I want requests over 120 minutes or more than 7 days ahead to be rejected, so that no one hoards scarce hardware.
As a student, I want to receive a unique reservation token on confirmation, so that I can prove my booking at the issue counter.
As a lab technician, I want to record date performed, next-due date and certificate ID against an instrument, so that every instrument's calibration state is on record.
As a faculty supervisor, I want an instrument to leave the bookable inventory the moment its next-due date passes, so that no reading is taken on an out-of-calibration instrument.
As a lab technician, I want calibration and penalty actions restricted to my role, so that students cannot alter their own records.
As a lab technician, I want to validate the student's reservation token before handing over an instrument, so that only the rightful booker takes it.
As a lab technician, I want expired, reused or wrong-instrument tokens rejected with a clear reason, so that I can refuse issue confidently at the counter.
As an auditor, I want check-out and check-in timestamps stored server-side against the reservation, so that a late return can be proven from the record.
As a lab technician, I want overdue duration computed automatically at check-in, so that I never have to judge lateness by hand.
As a student, I want a 30-minute grace window before a strike is recorded, so that a queue at the issue counter does not penalise me.
As a faculty supervisor, I want booking privileges suspended for 14 days on a third strike in 30 days, so that repeat offenders stop blocking lab capacity.

As an auditor, I want every reservation, calibration, custody and penalty event logged immutably with actor, action, timestamp and before/after state, so that a suspension can be contested with evidence.
As a student, I want to be told within 5 minutes if my future booking is voided by calibration expiry, so that I can rebook on another instrument in time.
As a student, I want to be notified within a minute of a strike or a suspension, so that I am never surprised by a blocked booking.
As a student, I want to cancel a reservation up to 2 hours before its start time, so that I am not penalised when my plans change.
As a student, I want to join the waitlist for a fully booked instrument-slot, so that I get a chance if someone cancels.
As a waitlisted student, I want a released slot offered to me in waitlist order with 30 minutes to accept, so that the offer is fair and does not stall on one person.
As a faculty supervisor, I want unused, uncancelled reservations marked NO_SHOW, so that ghost bookings are visible in utilisation data.
As a lab technician, I want to export 12 months of the audit log as CSV, so that I can answer an external audit without developer help.
As a student, I want exactly one of many simultaneous requests for the same slot to succeed within 200 ms, so that double-booking is impossible rather than merely unlikely.
As a faculty supervisor, I want to see booked versus actually used hours per instrument, so that I can find where lab capacity is being wasted.
As a faculty supervisor, I want to filter utilisation by date range and department, so that I can justify new equipment purchases with evidence.
